description: A Reeds-Shepp path is a shortest path for a car that drives forward and backward at unit speed and cannot turn tighter than a minimum radius. The car's state is a pose: a position and a heading. Reeds and Shepp showed that a shortest path always has at most five parts, each a circular arc at the minimum radius or a straight line, with optional changes of gear (*cusps*) between them. The crate moves the goal into the start's frame, scales it by the radius, evaluates the closed-form formula of each path family under its symmetries, and keeps the shortest result. Its length is a true distance (symmetric, with the triangle inequality), so you can use it as the metric of a sampling-based planner for car-like vehicles that may reverse.

papers.title: Optimal paths for a car that goes both forwards and backwards
